response: Rain has ended. Water still stands among the orchard roots. Across the valley Mara waits by the village windows. She was a child when the old city drowned; this orchard grew on the bank where the survivors arrived.

response: Water withdraws from the orchard roots and enters the hollow. A copper bell rises through the silt. Under its lip are the names of the drowned city. It is not an alarm: held close, it whispers each person once.
Mara comes to the cleared orchard. She recognizes Anwen, her mother, on the bell—and beside it, Rook. A line cast into the metal joins their names.
“They told me Rook shut the gate and left us,” she says. “Why would my mother’s name be joined to his?” She leaves the question beside the quiet bell. You can leave it there too.

knownStoryFacts.fact: On the exposed bell, Anwen’s name is joined to Rook’s by a cast line. Anwen was Mara’s mother. Mara was taught that Rook closed the city gate and abandoned the people behind it.

The voices speak to one another: Rook is holding the south ferry rope, Anwen the north. They send the children across first. One of those children is Mara. The gate closed against the river, not against the escaping children.

response: Air enters the bell. Every village window answers with a name no living mouth remembers. The river turns toward those voices. Water rises over the village doorsteps; the orchard stays clear.

“South rope holding,” says Rook. “North rope holding,” answers Anwen. Then, together: “The children first.” Mara hears her own name among the passengers. The closing gate was turned against the river; two people held the crossing open.

At the village windows, the old story of abandonment gives way to the sound of people helping one another. Now the same voices are calling water over those doorsteps. What you learned remains true while you decide what to make of that consequence.

response: Stone closes around the bell without altering a single name. The exact record is protected now. The voices cease. Water returns to its earth course; the city is no longer audible from the village windows.

Before the stone closes, its impression makes the inscription’s ordering legible. Anwen and Rook are at opposite ends of one ferry line. Below them are the names of children who crossed, including Mara. The bell was never only a list of the dead.
Mara traces the two ends of the line. “They held it together.” The exact record will stay here, even though the village will not hear the original voices from its windows.

action.intention: Leave both settlements safe beside the river, with the exact crossing record protected and the story of Anwen and Rook corrected.

report.perspective: AI player account only; no claim about human enjoyment
experienceSequence: Recognized the familiar safe hollow diversion and performed it without new mechanical uncertainty.
Reached the required checkpoint after clearing the orchard.
The joined names and apparent contradiction in the story of Rook gave me a specific reason to continue.
Declared continuation and chose air for spoken context, accepting the publicly known temporary flood.
The exchange answered my question: Anwen and Rook held the crossing while the children escaped.
Chose stone to preserve an exact record and restore safety and river contact.
Finished after two optional combinations because the adopted question was answered and the valley was in a satisfactory state.
noticedResponses: The cast line joins the name of a survivor mother to a person accused of abandonment.
The voices address each other and name Mara among the children, giving the revelation a specific human connection.
The archive distinguishes the people holding the ferry from those crossing; it is not only a list of the dead.
Previously learned facts remain known after the bell is sealed, so the village retains the correction without continuing to hear the original voices.
report.narrativeQuestion: Why are Anwen and Rook joined if Rook abandoned the city?
report.passageThatMattered: South rope holding / North rope holding / The children first. The paired voices make the joined inscription intelligible and connect the answer to Mara.
report.appreciation: The relation among the cast line, ferry rope and two people acting together gives the imagery coherence. This is story appreciation.
report.curiosity: I wanted the answer to one concrete contradiction. I chose spoken context over the other offered methods of knowing. That curiosity ended when the exchange answered it.
report.intentionSource: The world supplied the question and methods. I adopted the question as a reason to act; I did not invent an independent project or continue just to cover the revision. The test prompt elicited a decision about continuation but did not require it.
report.comparisonWithQuietClosure: In fun-bell-1 I had no reason to disturb exact private memory once both places were safe. Here a particular unresolved history gave me that reason. The revision changed my continuation behavior, while the safe initial combination remained just as obvious.
report.logicalChallenge: Low. I selected an interpretation method and a final memory form, but did not need to infer hidden causal rules or solve a difficult sequence. Air can supply its answer before stone repairs the flood, and learned facts persist. For my goal this makes hear-then-seal straightforward. The loss of ongoing voices mattered as a chosen value, but it did not block retaining the discovered truth.

meaningfulRepetition.scale: 0 none to 4 strong; AI stated willingness
meaningfulRepetition.explanation: Replaying the same answer would mainly be rereading. I have mild comparative interest in another interpretation, but no current project strong enough to restart for it.

report.automaticResolutionLoss: Automatically diverting the river would lose little challenge. Automatically choosing air then stone would remove authorship over what form of knowledge and final memory to keep, but much of the value I pursued could still be delivered as a written story. This play does not establish durable fun in repeated combinations.
report.actualStoppingReason: The specific adopted mystery was answered; the exact record was protected; both places were safe and river contact restored. I did not want more recipe completion or another memory transformation.
report.wantToDiscoverNext: No further question in this instance currently motivates action.
